strings.name: Jayati Ghosh
strings.role: Development economist and UMass Amherst professor
strings.summary: Indian development economist Jayati Ghosh studies globalization, employment, gender and inequality. After a long teaching career at Jawaharlal Nehru University, she moved to UMass Amherst in 2021. She contributes to international economic debate through research networks, policy advice and public writing.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Current and former roles, and joint and sole authorship, are distinguished. The ILO award follows the 2011 presentation record; policy views are attributed to their authors.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies globalization, employment and gender in development, contributing to public policy debate in emerging economies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Undergraduate and master’s education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned an honours BA in sociology at the University of Delhi in 1975 and an MA in economics at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 1977.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research training at Cambridge
strings.facts.f2.value: Earned an MPhil in economics in 1979 and a PhD in economics in 1983, both at Cambridge.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Development and labour research
strings.highlights.h1.text: Connects development economics with employment, gender and inequality in academic and public policy debate.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Collaborative inequality research
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-authored the 2025 G20 Global Inequality Report; its policy options are not equivalent to measures adopted by governments.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joint tariff commentary republished
strings.timeline.t1.text: IDEAs republished her article with C.P. Chandrasekhar on US tariffs and supply chains, noting original publication on September 29.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Contributed to the G20 inequality report
strings.timeline.t2.text: Co-authored the independent experts’ report, which is not an intergovernmentally adopted policy document.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Received the Galbraith Award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received the John Kenneth Galbraith Award from the Agricultural and Applied Economics Association.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Moved to UMass Amherst
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began serving as professor of economics; her previous JNU appointment had ended in 2020.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Received the ILO Decent Work Research Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received the prize at the Geneva ceremony; the ILO’s dated record is used rather than 2010 as listed in some biographies.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined India’s National Knowledge Commission
strings.timeline.t6.text: Served from 2005 to 2009, a historical policy advisory role.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Began teaching at JNU
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her CV records a progression from assistant professor to associate professor and professor, through 2020.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned a Cambridge economics PhD
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed the doctorate after her earlier economics MA and MPhil studies.
